implemented_requirements.requirement: Two-player Pong game with a graphical interface
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py creates a Tk root and instantiates Game(root); pong.py defines class Game that builds a canvas and runs the game loop.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Each player controls a vertical paddle, moving up and down
implemented_requirements.evidence: Paddle class stores up_key and down_key; left paddle uses "w"/"s", right paddle uses "Up"/"Down". Game.update calls left.move(self.keys) and right.move(self.keys) to adjust y position.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball bounces between the two paddles and off the top and bottom edges
implemented_requirements.evidence: Ball.update reverses vy when y <= 0 or y+BALL_SIZE >= HEIGHT. Game.collide detects paddle hits and Game.bounce changes vx/vy accordingly.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players score a point when the opponent misses the ball
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.update checks if ball.x + BALL_SIZE <= 0 (right scores) or ball.x >= WIDTH (left scores) and calls score_point(scorer).
Constant WIN_SCORE = 5; score_point sets self.winner and state "over" when scorer.score >= WIN_SCORE.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Reset the ball after each point
implemented_requirements.evidence: score_point calls self.ball.reset(self.serve_dir) when the game is not over, and Game.__init__ also calls ball.reset for the initial serve.

judge.summary: The provided code implements a functional two‑player Pong game using Tkinter. All core requirements—player‑controlled paddles, ball physics with wall and paddle collisions, scoring, a win condition, and ball reset after each point—are present and appear correct. The program is likely executable without modification, leading to a passing verdict.
